title: New Device Joined Network Alert
dataSources: UniFi controller events (`unifi:event`), Pi-hole query log (`pihole:query`), AdGuard Home (`adguard:query`), speedtest-cli results (`speedtest:result`), router/firewall syslog.
app: UniFi / router syslog, Pi-hole/AdGuard, and scheduled speedtests via HEC scripted inputs and the Universal Forwarder.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=unifi:event event_key="EVT_LU_Connected"
| stats earliest(_time) as first_seen by mac hostname
| eval age_hours=round((now()-first_seen)/3600,1)
| where age_hours<24
| sort - first_seen
description: Alerts when a device never seen before joins your Wi-Fi, catching both a neighbour on your password and a new gadget you forgot you set up.
value: A rogue device on your network is a real privacy and security concern; first-seen detection is a simple, effective tripwire.
implementation: Forward UniFi client-connect events; schedule hourly and alert on any newly seen MAC address.
visualization: Table of newly seen devices with first-seen time.
grandmaExplanation: It tells you when a device you have never seen before joins your Wi-Fi, like a neighbour guessing your password.
